research_question: Can a semantically sufficient runtime projection become physically invalid after materialization, and can replanning be triggered only by planner-relevant resource changes rather than every observation epoch?
hypotheses: A startup placement can become infeasible after runtime/page-cache/workspace materialization changes available RAM.
A planner-relevant resource certificate is a narrower invalidation surface than global observation epoch identity.
Replanning can change physical placement while preserving the exact FR-P9-001 semantic projection.
If a required backing tier disappears and RAM is insufficient, admission must fail closed rather than discard semantic atoms.
Resource replanning grants neither execution authority nor retry permission.
primary_oracles: irrelevant epoch-only change preserves the resource certificate and placement
post-materialization resource change invalidates the startup plan
the stale startup plan is physically infeasible under the post-materialization snapshot
replanning preserves the semantic atom set
replanning restores physical feasibility without current GENERATE-phase transfer
